newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares weaker in directionless market.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares weaker in directionless market.

text.p: Zimbabwe's industrial index lost 14.56 points to close at 10,042.41 on Wednesday, with brokers saying it needed direction to get it back on track.

"We'll have to look for a bit of good news and a potential source of direction should be the budget in July which will indicate the thrust of government spending for the next 18 months," one broker commented.
Analysts say high government spending has fuelled inflation, currently at 22.4 percent and interest rates, driving investors away from the stocks to the local money market.
Counters to lose on Wednesday included multi-industrial regional giant TZI which was down 20 cents at 1,020 while finance house Finhold shed 10 cents to 630.
Circle Cement eased 80 cents to 450, tyre firm NTS put off 50 to 300 cents, cool drink company Schweppes lost 35 cents to 310 and pharmaceutical group Caps were 25 cents weaker at 2,875.
But the secondary mining index added 4.13 points to 966.53 on the back of stronger deals in coal producer Wankie, up five cents to 570 while gold company Rio Tinto put on 50 cents to 2,050.
